ਸੰਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਰੇਣੁਕਾ ਲੈ ਮਾਥੈ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ: Seeking the dust of the saints' feet as the ultimate blessing, this act becomes the supreme treasure and the highest attainments. This physical gesture signifies complete surrender and the recognition of the saints' feet as the source of all spiritual wealth and liberation. Themes: surrender, devotion, spiritual wealth, saints' dust, highest attainments, ultimate blessing.
ਗੁਰਸਿਖਾਂ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਧੂੜਿ ਦੇਹਿ ਹਮ ਪਾਪੀ ਭੀ ਗਤਿ: This is a plea for refuge and transformation through the Guru's Sikhs, seeking their blessed dust as a means of spiritual elevation for a sinful self. It positions the Guru's followers as conduits of divine grace, whose presence can purify and elevate even the most degraded soul. Themes: divine refuge, spiritual transformation, Guru's Sikhs, grace, purification, sinful self, blessed dust, spiritual elevation.
ਕਰਉ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਭਗਤ ਜਨ ਧੂਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਲਾਵਉ ॥੩॥: This line expresses profound reverence for humble devotees, seeking their association to cultivate divine love. The speaker desires to join the sangat, applying the dust of their feet to their face as an act of supreme humility and surrender, believing this connection enables the singing of God's praises. Themes: humility, devotion, sangat (the company of the devout), surrender, divine love, spiritual association.
ਟਹਲ ਕਰਉ ਤੇਰੇ ਦਾਸ ਕੀ ਪਗ ਝਾਰਉ ਬਾਲ ॥:
This is an expression of devoted service, positioning the self as a humble servant performing menial acts for the Divine's devotee. It emphasizes the importance of selfless service (seva) and the spiritual value of honoring those connected to the Divine. The act of wiping feet with hair signifies total humility and surrender, suggesting that true devotion manifests in caring for the Guru's followers. The line instructs the devotee to find spiritual fulfillment in serving others.

Themes: seva (selfless service), humility, devotion to the Divine's followers, surrender, spiritual service, caring for the Guru's sangat (company of the devout)
ਕਰਿ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਧੂਰਿ ਦੇਹੁ ਸੰਤਨ ਕੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਇ:
The speaker petitions the Divine for grace, specifically requesting the dust of the saints' feet as a supreme blessing. This dust represents both ultimate refuge and the essence of divine connection, a tangible form of grace that grants peace. The act of seeking this dust is an expression of complete surrender and the highest form of spiritual yearning, positioning the dust as the mediator between the devotee and the Divine.

Themes: divine grace, surrender, saintly association, peace, refuge, spiritual yearning, humility, blessing
ਸੰਤਹ ਚਰਣ ਹਮਾਰੋ ਮਾਥਾ ਨੈਨ ਦਰਸੁ ਤਨਿ ਧੂਰਿ ਪਰ: This is an ardent expression of surrender and longing for the company of the saints, seeking physical prostration at their feet, visual absorption in their presence, and identification with the dust of their sanctuary as the ultimate state of devotion. Themes: surrender, longing, devotion, saints' company, physical prostration, divine vision, humility, refuge.
ਅਤਿ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਮਨਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਸਭਹੂ ਮਧਿ ਨਿਰਾਰੇ ॥:
This line addresses the Divine as the supreme beauty that captivates the soul, simultaneously present in all creation yet transcendent beyond it. The words of praise are not mere flattery but the very means of granting spiritual life, transforming the listener from a state of separation to one of divine recognition. The image of the Divine as both immanent and transcendent captures the paradox of being simultaneously everywhere and nowhere.

Themes: divine immanence, divine transcendence, transformative power of praise, captivation of the soul, paradox of presence, spiritual awakening, divine beauty, separation and union
ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਰੂਪੁ ਰੂੜੋ ਅਤਿ ਰੰਗ ਰੂੜੋ ਮੇ:
This is an expression of awe and devotion, praising the Divine's beauty through three distinct aspects: the naam (divine Name), form, and loving essence. The repetition of "so beautiful" emphasizes the overwhelming nature of this beauty, creating a sense of surrender and wonder. It is a direct address to the Divine, acknowledging the perfection that inspires devotion.

Themes: divine beauty, naam (divine Name), loving devotion, surrender, awe, perfection, direct address, overwhelming presence
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਰਸਾਲ ਤੂ ॥੧॥: The Divine is beautiful and the origin of all sweetness and joy. This is a declaration of the Divine's nature as the ultimate source of delight and the essence of beauty. The Divine is not merely beautiful but is the very source from which all beauty and sweetness flow. Themes: divine beauty, source of nectar, ultimate delight, essence of sweetness, origin of joy.
ਨੈਣ ਪਸੰਦੋ ਸੋਇ ਪੇਖਿ ਮੁਸਤਾਕ ਭਈ ॥:
The Divine form captivates the eyes, inducing a state of ecstatic enchantment through visual devotion. This is the effect of beholding the beloved, a mesmerizing love that overwhelms the senses and transports the devotee beyond worldly concerns. It describes the soul's response to divine beauty as a form of spiritual intoxication.

Themes: divine beauty, visual devotion, ecstatic love, spiritual enchantment, intoxication of the soul, gaze of the beloved, transcendent vision, naam (the divine Name) as form.
ਸੁੰਦਰ ਸੋਭਾ ਲਾਲ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਦਇਆਲ ਕੀ ਅਪਰ ਅਪਾਰਾ ਰ:
The Divine's beauty and glory emanate from boundless mercy, a presence that permeates all creation. This is not merely aesthetic beauty but the splendor of infinite, unconditional love that forms the foundation of existence. To recognize this beauty is to understand the nature of reality itself.

Themes: divine mercy, infinite glory, unconditional love, splendor of creation, nature of reality, foundation of existence, boundless compassion, permeating presence
ਅਪੁਨੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਕੀ ਆਪੇ ਰਾਖੈ ਆਪੇ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵੈ ॥:
The Divine personally safeguards His devotees and instills in them the practice of naam simran. This is an act of divine grace, not human effort, where the Lord both protects and guides His servants to spiritual remembrance. The Lord's protection is inseparable from His gift of naam, creating a cycle of divine care and human devotion.

Themes: divine grace, protection, naam simran, devotion, surrender, spiritual practice
ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਰਾਖੈ ਜੁਗਿ ਜੁਗਿ ਰਖਦਾ ਆ: The Divine Being safeguards the honor of His devotees across all ages, establishing their dignity as eternal. This is a declaration of divine protection and the honored status of the humble who surrender to the Divine. The Lord's preservation is not mere survival but the elevation of His devotees' worth before all creation. Themes: divine protection, devotee's honor, eternal guardianship, surrender, humility, dignity, Lord's presence, unwavering support.
ਭਗਤ ਤੇਰੇ ਸਭਿ ਪ੍ਰਾਣਪਤਿ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਮ ਤੂੰ ਭਗਤਨ ਕਾ: The Divine is the Beloved Lord of life for all devotees, who in turn are the Divine's Beloved. This establishes a reciprocal relationship of love between the Divine and the devotee, where the Divine sustains all life and is cherished by those who love, while the Divine cherishes them in return. Themes: Divine love, reciprocal devotion, Lord of life, beloved relationship, bhagat (devotee), pritam (beloved).
ਭਗਤਾ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਤੂੰ ਸੰਤਾ ਕੀ ਓਟ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਸਿਰਜਨ:
This line declares the Divine as the foundational support and refuge for the devotees and saints, positioning the Creator as the ultimate source of safety and protection. The Divine Name functions as both the tangible support and the spiritual shelter, emphasizing that true security comes only from the eternal Creator. The line establishes a relationship of dependence between the faithful and the Divine, highlighting the Creator's role as the unwavering foundation for those who seek refuge.

Themes: divine protection, refuge in the Divine, support for devotees, shelter for saints, Creator as foundation, security through faith, dependence on the eternal, relationship with the Divine.
ਹਰਿ ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਭਗਤ ਉਪਾਇਆ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਦਾ ਆਇਆ ਰਾਮ:
This line declares the Divine's continuous action across time: creating devotees in every age and safeguarding their honor. It frames this as a royal act of protection and preservation, emphasizing the Divine's unwavering commitment to the faithful. The Divine is both the originator of devotion and its eternal guardian.

Themes: divine protection, devotee preservation, timeless grace, honor safeguarding, royal sovereignty, eternal guardianship, unwavering support, spiritual continuity.
ਹਮਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਨ ਬਿਚਰਹੁ ਠਾਕੁਰ ਤੁਮ੍ਹ ਪੈਜ ਰਖਹੁ ਅ: The speaker pleads for divine mercy, abandoning claims to good deeds while seeking refuge in the Lord's honor. This is a posture of complete surrender, acknowledging human unworthiness while appealing to the Master's grace. The request to disregard karma is an admission of spiritual insufficiency, while preserving honor affirms the divine relationship. Themes: divine mercy, surrender, karma, grace, honor, refuge, humility, devotion.
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਨਿਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਕਰੇ ਕਬੂਲੁ ॥:
The human as a beggar constantly pleading for the divine Name (naam) receives acceptance from the Lord-Master. This describes the relationship between devotee and Divine as one of utter dependence and grace, where persistent supplication for naam is met with divine reception. The image of begging underscores humility before the Lord's sovereignty.

Themes: supplication, divine grace, naam, humility, acceptance, dependence, prayer, surrender
ਦੇਹਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੀਆ ਉਤਰੈ ਮਨ ਕੀ ਭੁਖ ॥:
This is a plea for the divine naam (the Name) as the remedy for both spiritual discontent and mental craving. The speaker positions naam as the sole satisfaction for the soul's emptiness and the mind's restless hunger, framing it as the essential substance for true contentment. The request implies that naam alone can quench the deepest human thirst.

Themes: divine Name, contentment, mind's hunger, spiritual fulfillment, seeking refuge, naam as sustenance, inner peace, devotion
ਜਾਚਿਕੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਜਾਚੈ ॥:
The soul, a beggar before the Divine, repeatedly pleads for the naam (divine Name), recognizing it as the only true refuge and sustenance. This line establishes a posture of complete humility and desperate dependence, framing the human condition as one of perpetual seeking for the only source of true nourishment and protection from the emptiness of worldly existence.

Themes: begging, divine Name, refuge, humility, dependence, sustenance, surrender, longing
ਕਰਹੁ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿਦੇ ਅਪਨਾ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਵਹ:
This is a direct plea for divine grace to enable the practice of naam (the divine Name). The speaker seeks assistance from Gopal and Govind (Divine protectors and creators) to overcome obstacles in simran (loving remembrance), positioning this as an act of dependence rather than self-generated effort. The request frames spiritual practice as a gift requiring divine intervention.

Themes: divine mercy, spiritual practice, dependence on the Divine, chanting the Name, seeking assistance, surrender, protection, devotion
ਜਾਚਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਦੇਹਿ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥:
The speaker positions themselves as a beggar not for material goods but for the Lord's grace (khar), which is the infinite Word. This is a plea for divine favor, expressing humility and total dependence on the Beloved's mercy. The image of begging underscores the soul's absolute need for the Divine Name (naam) to be granted as a gift.

Themes: divine grace, humility, begging for the Name, soul's dependence, mercy, surrender, gift of the Word, unconditional love
ਦਰਿ ਮੰਗਤੁ ਜਾਚੈ ਦਾਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਦੀਜੈ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਕਰਿ:
The speaker positions themselves as a beggar at the Divine door, seeking refuge through charity and mercy. This posture of complete surrender and dependence is the core practice, where naam (the divine Name) is the ultimate gift received through grace. The act of begging is not just a request but a recognition of one's absolute need for the Divine.

Themes: surrender, begging, grace, refuge, dependence, mercy, naam, divine charity
ਮਉਲਿਓ ਮਨੁ ਤਨੁ ਹੋਇਓ ਹਰਿਆ ਏਕ ਬੂੰਦ ਜਿਨਿ ਪਾਈ: The mind and body flourish when even a single drop of the divine Name's nectar is received. This transformation is both a spiritual awakening and a physical renewal, describing the profound effect of naam (the divine Name) on one's entire being. The line celebrates the power of this connection to revitalize the self. Themes: divine nectar, spiritual transformation, naam, inner flourishing, renewal, receiving grace
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਤ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਰਾਤਾ ॥: Absorbing the divine essence (ras) through naam (the divine Name) results in permanent spiritual coloring. This absorption is not momentary but eternal, transforming the being's fundamental nature. The act of drinking this nectar is an ongoing process of internalizing the divine, leading to an unchangeable state of divine connection. Themes: divine absorption, eternal transformation, naam as nectar, spiritual coloring, permanent divine connection, internalization of the divine.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਰਸੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਅਹਿਨਿਸਿ ਪੂਰਨ:
This line instructs the devotee to sing the Lord's praises continuously, as this ambrosial kirtan is the essence of spiritual life. The teeka clarifies that this internal singing, not external performance, is what causes the divine sound-current (naad) to resonate within one being day and night, creating perpetual spiritual bliss. The kirtan is both the method and the result, a practice that generates its own reward.

Themes: ambrosial praise, internal kirtan, divine sound-current, perpetual spiritual bliss, continuous remembrance, selfless devotion, inner ananda, naam simran.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸਨਾ ਪੀਉ ਪਿਆਰੀ ॥:
This instruction directs the tongue to imbibe the divine Name, which grants spiritual life. The metaphor of drinking ambrosia transforms the act of naam simran into a life-sustaining nourishment, positioning the tongue as the primary instrument for receiving this essence. The command to drink establishes a relationship of dependency and absorption with the Name, the source of eternal sustenance.

Themes: tongue as spiritual instrument, naam as ambrosial nectar, divine nourishment, simran as absorption, life-giving Name, spiritual sustenance, drinking the divine, transformation through remembrance.
ਤੇਰਾ ਜਨੁ ਰਾਮ ਰਸਾਇਣਿ ਮਾਤਾ ॥:
This line expresses a state of divine intoxication where the devotee finds complete absorption in the essence of the Divine Name. It describes the soul's surrender as a humble servant overwhelmed by the sweetness of naam (the divine Name), finding ultimate fulfillment in this loving remembrance. The image of intoxication conveys both ecstatic union and the loss of separate selfhood.

Themes: divine intoxication, humble surrender, absorption in naam, ecstatic union, sweetness of the Divine, loss of self, loving remembrance, devotion as fulfillment
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਆ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੀ ਹਮ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਟਹੁ ਕ:
The Guru's Word enables drinking the ambrosial essence of naam, resulting in complete surrender to the Divine. This state is both a spiritual nourishment and a total offering of the self to the Divine Name. The line describes the transformative power of the Guru's teachings to turn the seeker into an offering through the experience of naam's sweetness.

Themes: Guru's Word, ambrosial essence, surrender to Naam, spiritual nourishment, self-offering, transformative teaching, naam experience, complete devotion
ਰਸੁ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਰਸੁ ਅਤਿ ਭਲਾ ਕਿਤੁ ਬਿਧਿ: The divine Name is the supreme essence granting spiritual life, a nectar that cannot be obtained through ritual or effort. This essence is the ultimate goal, yet its attainment remains mysterious. The line expresses a profound yearning to directly experience this ambrosia, questioning how one can taste this divine essence. Themes: divine essence, spiritual longing, naam (divine Name), attainment, mystery, nectar, supreme goal.
ਹਰਿ ਰਸੁ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥: This instruction commands immersion in the divine essence through naam (the divine Name) as the sole refuge, positioning this practice as the fundamental purpose of human life. It presents the absorption of the Lord's sweetness as both a direct command and the ultimate fulfillment, achievable only through complete surrender and loving remembrance (simran). Themes: divine essence, surrender, loving remembrance, purpose of life, refuge, sweetness, absorption, liberation.
ਬਿਖੈ ਬਨੁ ਫੀਕਾ ਤਿਆਗਿ ਰੀ ਸਖੀਏ ਨਾਮੁ ਮਹਾ ਰਸੁ:
This line instructs the mind to abandon the insipid water of worldly corruption and instead drink the supreme nectar of naam (the divine Name), which provides true fulfillment. It presents a stark choice between spiritual emptiness and divine nourishment, urging the seeker to reject maya (worldly attachment) in favor of the eternal sweetness of simran (loving remembrance). The contrast between tasteless water and nectar emphasizes the superior value of spiritual practice over worldly pursuits.

Themes: spiritual nourishment, rejection of worldly corruption, divine sweetness, remembrance over attachment, supreme taste, eternal fulfillment, choice between paths, seeking the Name
ਕਬੀਰ ਬਿਰਹੁ ਭੁਯੰਗਮੁ ਮਨਿ ਬਸੈ ਮੰਤੁ ਨ ਮਾਨੈ ਕ: The mind poisoned by separation from the Divine cannot be healed by any ritual or mantra. This separation is a venomous serpent that renders all spiritual practices ineffective. The state of divine longing is so consuming that external remedies fail; only the Guru's sanctuary can neutralize this poison. Themes: divine longing, spiritual ineffectiveness, Guru's refuge, separation poison, mantra failure, mind's vulnerability
ਹਰਿ ਬਿਨੁ ਕਿਉ ਜੀਵਾ ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਈ ॥:
The soul's existence is fundamentally dependent on the Divine Name; without it, life becomes anxious and meaningless. This is not a question but a declaration of spiritual necessity, expressing the inextricable bond between the individual consciousness and the Supreme. The Divine Name is the essential sustainer of the soul's peace and purpose.

Themes: divine dependence, soul's sustenance, spiritual anxiety, naam as essential, mother as metaphor, refuge in the Divine, life's meaning, separation from God.
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਮਿਲਬੇ ਕਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਮਨਿ ਲਾਗੀ ॥:
This line expresses the profound yearning of the devotee's soul for union with the Divine, describing the spontaneous arising of loving affection as the essential first step toward that meeting. This affection is not mere emotion but the active force driving spiritual seeking, positioning the mind in a state of receptive longing that precedes divine encounter. The line establishes the foundational emotional state necessary for all true spiritual pursuit.

Themes: divine yearning, loving devotion, spiritual seeking, mind's preparation, spontaneous affection, soul's longing, union with the Beloved
ਹਰਿ ਦਰਸਨ ਕਉ ਮੇਰਾ ਮਨੁ ਬਹੁ ਤਪਤੈ ਜਿਉ ਤ੍ਰਿਖਾ: The mind intensely yearns for the Divine Vision, burning with longing like a thirsty person without water. This is not mere desire but a state of parched desperation, where the soul's thirst for the Divine presence exceeds all physical needs. The image of thirst conveys both the intensity of spiritual longing and the soul's dependence on the Divine for fulfillment. Themes: spiritual longing, divine vision, soul's thirst, dependence on the Divine, parched desperation, seeking the Beloved.
ਬਾਝਹੁ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਸਾਰੇ ਏਕਲੜੀ ਕੁਰਲਾਏ ॥: This expresses utter abandonment and the resulting solitary lament, positioning the Divine as the sole source of care in an indifferent world. The speaker is isolated in a wilderness, crying out because only the Divine Beloved offers true connection and refuge. This is a declaration of spiritual desolation and the exclusive refuge found in the Divine. Themes: Divine love, isolation, worldly neglect, spiritual longing, refuge, solitude, lament, divine care.
ਮਨਿ ਬੈਰਾਗੁ ਭਇਆ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਦੇਖਣੈ ਕਾ ਚਾਉ ॥: The mind has achieved detachment from worldly attachment (maya) through the divine Name (naam), generating an intense longing for the Vision of the Divine. This state is the fruit of loving remembrance (simran), a transformation where the devotee's consciousness turns entirely toward the Divine presence, forsaking all other attachments. Themes: detachment, longing for divine vision, transformation of consciousness, fruit of naam, maya, simran, divine love.
ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਚਿਰੀ ਵਿਛੁੰਨਿਆ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਬਦਿ ਗੁਰੂ ਪ੍: This is a plea for reunion with the Divine, expressing the pain of separation and the desire for absorption through the Guru's Shabad. It frames the human heart as a home waiting for the Divine to inhabit, using the Guru's Word as the means to dissolve the illusion of separation and achieve union. Themes: longing, reunion, divine absorption, Guru's Word, heart as home, dissolution of separation.
ਪਿਰ ਦੋਸੁ ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਹ ਦਾਤੇ ਹਉ ਵਿਛੁੜੀ ਬੁਰਿਆਰ:
The speaker absolves the Divine of blame for their separation, acknowledging their own flawed actions as the cause. This is a confession of personal responsibility in the face of divine grace, a stark admission that worldly attachments create distance from the source of all peace. The Husband Lord remains blameless; the fault lies entirely with the individual's mistaken choices.

Themes: divine grace, personal responsibility, separation from the Divine, flawed actions, worldly attachment, surrender, confession, Husband Lord
ਆਉ ਜੀ ਤੂ ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਸੁਨਾਵਨਾ:
The speaker urgently invites the Divine to reside within their heart, enabling them to hear the Lord's praises. This is a plea for divine presence and the grace of experiencing naam (the divine Name) through simran (loving remembrance), transforming the self into a vessel for divine worship. The heart is the temple where this sacred listening occurs.

Themes: divine invitation, heart as temple, hearing praises, grace of naam, simran, longing for union, worship through listening, surrender to the Divine.
ਆਉ ਹਮਾਰੈ ਰਾਮ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਜੀਉ ॥:
This is an urgent invitation and a plea for divine union, expressing deep longing and surrender. The speaker calls the Divine Beloved to take residence within their heart, seeking not distant worship but intimate presence. It is a movement from separation to communion, a yearning for the Divine to become the inner reality. The line functions as both a prayer and a declaration of where true belonging is found.

Themes: divine union, heart as sanctuary, intimate presence, surrender, longing, beloved Lord, inner residence, prayer of invitation
ਬਿਨਵੰਤਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਇਆ ਧਾਰਹੁ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਨਾਹ ਪਿਆਰ: The soul pleads for the Divine's mercy to enter its home, the human heart, as a beloved husband dwells with his beloved. This is an urgent request for union with the Divine, emphasizing the soul's longing and the Lord's grace as essential for spiritual fulfillment. Themes: divine union, soul's longing, mercy, grace, beloved husband, heart as home, naam, simran.
ਮੋਹਨ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹੁ ਕਰਉ ਜੋਦਰੀਆ ॥:
This is a prayer of longing and surrender, inviting the Divine to take residence within the devotee's heart. The "house" is the inner self, a sanctuary made empty by worldly attachment, now offered as a dwelling for the Divine presence. It is an act of complete surrender, seeking union by making one's inner being a home for the beloved. The plea is intimate, personal, and transformative, asking the Lord to inhabit the very core of one's being.

Themes: divine presence, inner sanctuary, surrender, longing, heart as temple, personal prayer, union with the Divine, emptying of self
ਹਮ ਘਰਿ ਸਾਜਨ ਆਏ ॥:
The Divine Friend has manifested within my heart-home, transforming the inner space into a sanctuary of divine presence. This is not merely visitors but the arrival of the Beloved, making the body a temple through this intimate union. The soul recognizes this as its true purpose: to become the dwelling place for the Divine.

Themes: divine presence, inner home, manifestation, union with the Beloved, heart as temple, soul's purpose, intimate connection, sacred dwelling
ਪਹਿਲੈ ਪਹਰੈ ਫੁਲੜਾ ਫਲੁ ਭੀ ਪਛਾ ਰਾਤਿ ॥:
This line describes spiritual progression through the watches of night. The early hours of devotion are like flowers—beautiful beginnings—while the deepest communion with the Divine brings the fruit of amrit (nectar of immortality). It instructs that true fulfillment requires moving beyond initial stages to sustained naam (divine Name) simran (loving remembrance). The image of flowers and fruit represents the journey from preliminary practice to ultimate union.

Themes: spiritual progression, stages of devotion, naam simran, amrit, divine union, night watches, preliminary practice, ultimate fulfillment
ਕਬੀਰ ਸੂਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਉਠਿ ਕਿ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਮੁਰਾਰਿ:
This is a sharp rebuke to the sleeping self, questioning why one wastes life lost in worldly attachment (maya) instead of rising to loving remembrance (simran) of the Divine. It frames spiritual laziness as a dangerous slumber from which one must awaken to pursue the divine Name (naam). The image of rising from sleep represents the urgent need for spiritual awakening.

Themes: spiritual awakening, worldly attachment, divine remembrance, wasted life, self-rebuke, urgency of practice, overcoming lethargy, company of the devout (sangat)
ਪਰਭਾਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੇ ਚਰਣ ਧਿਆਇ ॥:
This instruction directs the devotee to begin the day with spiritual discipline by practicing naam (the divine Name) through simran (loving remembrance) and focusing on the Guru's teachings with humility. The act of meditating on the Guru's feet represents both a physical posture of surrender and a mental state of devotion, anchoring the practitioner in divine remembrance to counteract worldly distractions. This daily practice establishes a foundation of spiritual awareness and connection.

Themes: morning devotion, simran (loving remembrance), surrender to the Guru, naam (the divine Name), spiritual discipline, humility, daily practice, refuge in the Guru.
ਝਾਲਾਘੇ ਉਠਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਿ ਨਿਸਿ ਬਾਸੁਰ ਆਰਾਧਿ ॥:
This instruction commands the initiate to structure their life around divine remembrance, rising at the ambrosial hour to begin naam (the divine Name) simran (loving remembrance) and continuing this worship perpetually. It establishes a rhythm of consciousness that positions the devotee in constant adoration, transforming mundane time into sacred practice by anchoring every moment to the Divine presence.

Themes: spiritual discipline, daily practice, divine remembrance, constant worship, ambrosial hours, surrender to the Divine, structured devotion, overcoming sloth
ਬਾਬੀਹਾ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਵੇਲੈ ਬੋਲਿਆ ਤਾਂ ਦਰਿ ਸੁਣੀ ਪ:
The rainbird's pre-dawn call is a metaphor for the devotee's naam simran, a plea that reaches the Divine Court. This image establishes that sincere spiritual practice, even in darkness, is always heard and answered. The rainbird's natural song becomes a model for human devotion, showing how the soul's yearning connects with the Divine without intermediaries.

Themes: divine hearing, pre-dawn devotion, natural metaphor for prayer, soul's yearning, acceptance of prayer, connection with the Divine, bird imagery, spiritual practice
ਛਾਤੀ ਸੀਤਲ ਮਨੁ ਸੁਖੀ ਛੰਤ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਇ ॥:
This line describes the transformative effect of singing God's praises, which cools the heated heart and brings peace to the restless mind. It presents devotional singing (kirtan) as the direct means to achieve inner tranquility by focusing the mind on naam (the divine Name), thereby quenching the fires of worldly attachment (maya). The cooling of the chest is both a physical sensation and a metaphor for emotional calm.

Themes: devotional singing, inner peace, cooling of passion, focus on the divine, tranquility of mind, refuge in praise, overcoming restlessness, spiritual comfort
ਜੋਗੁ ਬਨਿਆ ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਈ ॥੧॥: This is a declaration of union with the Divine achieved through devotional singing. The act of kirtan (singing praises) is presented as the method of yoga (union), transforming worship into a direct spiritual experience. The teeka clarifies this dual blessing: worldly comfort and spiritual liberation both arise from this focused remembrance. Themes: kirtan, yoga, union, remembrance, devotion, liberation, comfort, divine presence
ਹਉ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਕਰਉ ॥:
This is a declaration of constant devotion, an instruction to maintain unceasing remembrance of the Divine through naam (the divine Name) and kirtan (singing praises). It describes the ideal spiritual state as one of continuous worship, a practice that transforms the devotee's entire existence into an offering. The line establishes this as the purpose of human life, a complete surrender of time to the Divine presence.

Themes: constant remembrance, unceasing worship, divine praise, surrender of time, naam, kirtan, devotion, spiritual practice
ਰੁਣ ਝੁਣੋ ਸਬਦੁ ਅਨਾਹਦੁ ਨਿਤ ਉਠਿ ਗਾਈਐ ਸੰਤਨ ਕ: This instruction commands rising early to sing the unstruck sound current of the divine Word in the company of the devout, transforming worship into a sweet, harmonious melody praising the Divine. It establishes a daily spiritual practice of collective singing to cultivate divine connection and remembrance. Themes: daily discipline, congregational worship, divine sound, naam meditation, sangat, simran, devotional practice.
ਸਾਧੋ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕੇ ਗੁਨ ਗਾਵਉ ॥:
This is an instruction to the devout to continuously sing the praises of the Divine. It establishes a devotional practice as the essential activity for the seeker, framing worship as an ongoing act of remembrance rather than a ritual. The line directs the mind toward naam through the practice of simran, positioning this as the primary purpose of human life.

Themes: devotional practice, continuous remembrance, divine praise, spiritual instruction, Sikh worship, naam, simran
ਨਿਰਬਾਣ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਗਾਵਹੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਕਾ ਨਿਮਖ ਸਿਮਰਤ ਜ: This line instructs to sing the praises of the Creator in a state of desirelessness, as even a moment of naam simran through this kirtan liberates one from worldly vices. The kirtan is both an act of worship and a method of meditation, with its salvific power stemming from the focused remembrance of the Divine. Themes: desirelessness, divine praise, meditation, liberation, remembrance, salvation, kirtan, vices.
ਮਨ ਮੀਠ ਤੁਹਾਰੋ ਕੀਓ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥:
The mind finds sweetness in all of the Divine's actions, regardless of their nature. This is a state of complete surrender where the devotee accepts every circumstance as sweet will, having abandoned any personal claim to superiority or entitlement. This acceptance transforms suffering into sweetness through naam (the divine Name) and simran (loving remembrance).

Themes: divine will, acceptance, surrender, mind's transformation, naam, simran, relinquishing ego, finding sweetness in all circumstances
ਮੀਤ ਕੇ ਕਰਤਬ ਕੁਸਲ ਸਮਾਨਾ ॥੧॥:
The Divine Friend's actions bring comfort and joy, reflecting a relationship of mutual delight where the Creator's works are experienced as blessings. This establishes a foundation of trust and affection in the divine-human connection, positioning the Creator as both benefactor and intimate companion. The line affirms that recognizing the Divine in daily life transforms ordinary experiences into sources of spiritual contentment.

Themes: divine friendship, comfort in creation, mutual delight, trust in the Divine, spiritual contentment, recognition of the Creator in daily life
ਸਰਬ ਸੁਖ ਆਨੰਦ ਮੰਗਲ ਰਸ ਮਾਨਿ ਗੋਬਿੰਦੈ ਆਗਿਓ ॥: This line declares that complete surrender to the Divine Will is the source of all peace, joy, and happiness. The state of bliss comes not from worldly pursuits but from accepting God's sweetness as the ultimate good. True contentment is found in this submission, which transforms all experiences into blessings. Themes: surrender, divine will, bliss, contentment, acceptance, peace, joy, happiness.
ਖਿਨ ਮਹਿ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪਨਹਾਰਾ ਆਪਨ ਹਾਥਿ ਮਤਾਤ ॥੧॥:
The Divine instantly creates and annihilates all existence, holding every decision and outcome within absolute control. This is a declaration of divine sovereignty over creation's permanence and destruction, emphasizing that all events occur solely by the Divine will. The image of holding matters in hands represents both intimate care and absolute authority over cosmic processes.

Themes: divine sovereignty, creation and destruction, absolute will, cosmic control, omnipotence, fate, divine power, universal governance.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੧॥: This line instructs the mind to continuously dwell on the naam, the divine Name, as this loving remembrance (simran) ensures all actions align with divine will and find resolution. The teeka emphasizes that constant remembrance of the Lord resolves all affairs, making the naam both the method and the guarantee of successful, purposeful action. Themes: divine remembrance, mind control, action resolution, purposeful living, naam meditation, divine will.
ਕਾਰਜੁ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਪੂਰਾ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ:
This line instructs the mind to sing the divine qualities, promising that complete surrender through naam simran resolves all affairs. The repetition of Har emphasizes constant remembrance, while the teeka clarifies this focused worship ensures divine grace. The mind is directed to shift from worldly concerns to devotional practice, trusting that this surrender brings fulfillment.

Themes: devotional surrender, divine grace, mind's focus, naam simran, maya detachment, divine qualities, spiritual resolution, remembrance practice
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧਣਾ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਆਵੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥੮॥:
This line instructs that the practice of naam simran (loving remembrance of the Divine Name) is the essential action through which all human purposes are fulfilled. It presents naam not as mere repetition but as the transformative work that aligns life with its divine purpose, resolving all affairs by connecting the individual to the source of existence. The line declares this as the fundamental teaching for successful human life.

Themes: Divine remembrance, purposeful action, life's fulfillment, spiritual practice, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance)
ਸਭੇ ਕਾਜ ਸਵਾਰਿਐ ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੰਦਾ ॥੭॥: Divine pleasure resolves all affairs. When the Divine is pleased, all tasks find completion. This is a declaration of surrender, where the devotee's success depends entirely on Divine will. It describes the state of being where worldly concerns dissolve in acceptance of the Divine plan. Themes: divine will, surrender, resolution of affairs, acceptance, dependence, grace.
ਸਗਲ ਮਨੋਰਥ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੋਏ ਕਦੇ ਨ ਹੋਇ ਦੁਖਾਲਾ ਜੀਉ:
This line declares a state of complete fulfillment where all desires vanish and suffering ends. It describes the result of naam simran, where the devotee's every need is met by the Divine, transforming worldly longing into eternal contentment. The absence of sorrow is the natural consequence of this union, a state of permanent peace achieved through surrender to the Divine will.

Themes: fulfillment of desires, end of suffering, divine contentment, naam simran, surrender to will, eternal peace, transformation of longing, absence of sorrow
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਆਧਾਰੁ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਆਸਰਾ ॥:
The lotus feet of the Divine serve as both the foundation and refuge for devotees, providing ultimate support in the journey of life. This image conveys complete surrender and dependence, framing the Divine as the only true anchor against life's storms. The lotus symbolizes purity and transcendence, while the feet represent accessibility and relationship, making the Divine both approachable and supreme.

Themes: divine refuge, lotus feet, surrender, support, foundation, devotion, humility, protection
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸੇਵੀ ਰਿਦ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਗੁਰ ਪੂਰੇ ਕੈ ਆਧਾਰਿ:
This instruction directs one to focus on the divine presence within the heart while relying on the Guru's support as a foundation. It establishes an internal spiritual practice of contemplation anchored in external guidance, creating a dual path of inner focus and outer reliance. The lotus feet represent both the accessible divine and the object of devotion, while the Guru provides essential stability for this internal worship.

Themes: divine presence, internal focus, Guru's support, contemplative practice, spiritual foundation, heart-centered devotion, dual path of worship
ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਰੀਤਿ ਸੰਤਨ ਮਨਿ ਆਵਏ ਜੀਉ: This line establishes the core practice of the Saints: a loving discipline focused on the Divine presence, which manifests as a reverent relationship with the Lord's Lotus Feet. This discipline is not mere intellectual assent but a settled state of mind, an internalized code of conduct that structures the Saint's entire being around devotion. Themes: Lotus Feet, Divine presence, Loving discipline, Reverent relationship, Settled state of mind, Internalized code of conduct, Devotion.
ਬੋਹਿਥੜਾ ਹਰਿ ਚਰਣ ਮਨ ਚੜਿ ਲੰਘੀਐ ॥:
The mind must board the vessel of the Divine Lotus Feet to cross over the ocean of worldly existence. This is a direct command to the self to seek refuge in the Lord, positioning the Divine as both a safe ship and the means of liberation from maya. The line functions as urgent instruction, offering the only path to safety from the cycle of birth and death.

Themes: refuge, surrender, liberation, crossing over, divine feet, mind's instruction, salvation, escape from maya.
ਹਰਿ ਚਰਨ ਕਮਲ ਮਨੁ ਬੇਧਿਆ ਕਿਛੁ ਆਨ ਨ ਮੀਠਾ ਰਾਮ: The mind finds its only true refuge in the Lord's Lotus Feet, surrendering to their divine presence. This state of absorption renders all worldly pleasures tasteless, as the sweetness of naam (the divine Name) alone satisfies the soul. The mind, once captivated by the Lord's grace, cannot find delight in any other attachment. Themes: surrender, divine sweetness, detachment from maya (worldly attachment), naam, refuge, mind's focus.
ਪੀ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਆਘਾਨਿਆ ਗੁਰਿ ਅਮਰੁ ਕਰਾਇਆ ॥੨॥:
This line describes the transformative power of the Guru's instruction, which grants immortality by enabling one to drink the amrit (nectar) of naam (divine Name). This spiritual nourishment satisfies the soul completely, liberating it from the cycles of death, old age, and suffering. The Guru acts as the conduit for this divine gift, facilitating the devotee's union with the eternal.

Themes: nectar, immortality, Guru's grace, spiritual liberation, eternal life, naam, satisfaction, deathlessness
ਜਿਨ੍ਹ ਪੀਆ ਸੇ ਮਸਤ ਭਏ ਹੈ ਤੂਟੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਫਾਹੇ ॥: Divine Name's nectar intoxicates the soul, dissolving all attachments to worldly illusion. This state of divine intoxication severs the shackles of maya, liberating the consciousness from its self-imposed limitations. The metaphor of drinking represents the complete absorption in naam, simran, and sangat, which results in ultimate freedom. Themes: divine intoxication, liberation from attachment, naam as nectar, dissolution of maya, soul's freedom, spiritual absorption.
ਹਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਸੋ ਚਖੈ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨਾ ॥੨॥:
This line instructs the mind to seek the divine Name as the life-giving ambrosia. It positions the human purpose as consuming naam (the divine Name), which grants spiritual life and liberation. The mind is directed to this practice as the essential nourishment for the soul, contrasting it with worldly attachment (maya). The image of tasting ambrosia represents the transformative experience of simran (loving remembrance).

Themes: divine nectar, mind's instruction, spiritual nourishment, naam as life, liberation from maya, soul's purpose, simran as consumption, ambrosial experience
ਗੁਰਿ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਚੋਇਆ ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀ:
The Guru has bestowed the life-giving nectar of naam (divine Name) upon the speaker, reviving their spiritually dead soul. This act transforms the individual from a state of spiritual death to eternal life, emphasizing the Guru's power to grant spiritual rebirth through the divine Word. The Guru's instruction is the means to overcome spiritual death and attain true life.

Themes: Guru's grace, spiritual rebirth, naam (divine Name) as nectar, transformation from death to life, Guru as life-giver, overcoming spiritual death, divine instruction, eternal life through Guru.
ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਮਿਲਿ ਪੀਵਹੁ ਭਾਈ ॥: The divine Name is ambrosial treasure, a nectarian essence to be collectively imbibed through sangat (the company of the devout). This is an urgent instruction to seek and internalize naam (the divine Name) as the sole sustenance for the soul, presented as a shared, life-giving drink that liberates from worldly attachment. Themes: ambrosial treasure, collective imbibition, divine essence, soul's sustenance, liberation from maya, sangat, naam as nectar.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟਿਓਨੁ ਫਿਰਿ ਜੋਨਿ ਨ ਪਾਏ ॥:
The Divine eradicates the terror of birth and death cycles, liberating the soul from reincarnation. This liberation represents the ultimate spiritual victory, achieved through naam (the divine Name) and simran (loving remembrance), breaking the endless cycle of suffering and rebirth. The soul attains eternal peace by surrendering to the Divine will.

Themes: liberation from reincarnation, eradication of fear of death, spiritual victory through naam, breaking the cycle of birth and death, eternal peace, surrender to Divine will, freedom from worldly suffering, attainment of moksha.
ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਭਉ ਲਥਾ ॥੨੦॥:
The mind achieves natural stillness, leading to divine union and liberation from existential fear. This state of intuitive poise grants direct experience of the Divine, dissolving the terror of mortality. The stillness that allows naam (the divine Name) to be realized also provides refuge from maya (worldly attachment) and its consequences. This liberation is both a spiritual state and a psychological release from the fear of death.

Themes: divine union, fearlessness, intuitive stillness, liberation from mortality, naam realization, maya transcendence, spiritual peace, death's defeat
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭਉ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਨ ਕਾ ਸਬਦੁ ਜਪਿ ॥: The humble servant's Word destroys the terror of birth and death, providing refuge from existential fear through loving remembrance. This instruction declares that the divine Name, when contemplated in the company of the devout, severs the cycle of rebirth by eradicating worldly attachment. Themes: fear of death, divine refuge, loving remembrance, company of the devout, liberation from rebirth, worldly attachment, humble servant, divine Word.
ਨ ਦਨੋਤਿ ਜਸਮਰਣੇਨ ਜਨਮ ਜਰਾਧਿ ਮਰਣ ਭਇਅੰ ॥੧॥ ਰ:
Meditation on the Divine Name eliminates the suffering of birth, aging, and death by severing attachment to worldly existence. This practice transforms human life from a cycle of fear into one of spiritual freedom, as loving remembrance of the Divine dissolves the illusion of separation. The teeka clarifies that meditation specifically counters the anxiety of mortality and decay.

Themes: naam (divine Name), simran (loving remembrance), maya (worldly attachment), liberation from fear, meditation, dissolution of suffering, spiritual freedom, overcoming mortality.
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਦੁਖੁ ਕਾਟੀਐ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਚੂਕੈ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਕਾਣੇ:
This line declares that the suffering of birth and death is eliminated through divine love, which also removes the terror of death's messenger. The teeka clarifies this occurs in the company of the devout, where lifelong suffering is cut away and the dread of mortality vanishes. This is a statement of liberation from existential fear through loving devotion.

Themes: liberation from suffering, elimination of death anxiety, divine love as refuge, company of the devout, transcendence of mortality, cutting away of worldly pain
ਜਨਮ ਮਰਣ ਭੈ ਲਾਥੇ ॥੪॥੨॥੫੨॥: The speaker has been liberated from existential terror regarding birth and death. This is not mere absence of fear but a profound state of spiritual freedom achieved through naam (the divine Name) and simran (loving remembrance), where the cycle of rebirth no longer holds power. The mind finds peace in surrendering to the Divine presence, which erases the fundamental anxieties of human existence. Themes: liberation from fear, divine refuge, spiritual freedom, overcoming existential dread, surrender to the Divine, naam (the divine Name), simran (loving remembrance)
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੈ ਆਸਰੈ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਸਿਉ ਰੰਗੁ ਲਾਏ ॥:
The line establishes the sangat (the company of the devout) as the essential foundation for developing divine love. It presents this not as optional fellowship but as the necessary support structure that enables a devotee to establish a loving connection with the Divine. This connection is described as a profound emotional and spiritual transformation, a falling in love that occurs only within the context of collective devotion.

Themes: sangat, divine love, spiritual support, collective devotion, connection with the Divine, foundation of faith
ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗਿ ਤਰੀਜੈ ਸਾਗਰੁ ਕਟੀਐ ਜਮ ਕੀ ਫਾਸਾ ਜੀ:
This line instructs that the sangat (the company of the devout) provides the means to escape the world-ocean of maya (worldly attachment), cutting the noose of death. The sangat is the vessel for liberation, transforming the cycle of birth and death into a crossing. By joining the holy, one achieves salvation and breaks free from divine judgment.

Themes: sangat, liberation, maya, death, salvation, crossing, divine judgment, company of the devout
ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਕੀ ਭੀਰ ਜਉ ਪਾਈ ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਸੰਗਿ:
The line describes the transformative power of sangat (the company of the devout), where joining the holy assembly leads directly to divine union. This is not merely meeting God but becoming one with the Divine through shared spiritual practice. The assembly acts as a crucible where worldly attachment dissolves and the divine presence is realized. The experience is presented as inevitable and complete for those who seek it.

Themes: divine union, transformative community, spiritual practice, dissolution of ego, presence of the Divine, shared devotion, path to realization
ਸੰਤਤ ਹੀ ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਸੰਗ ਸੁਰੰਗ ਰਤੇ ਜਸੁ ਗਾਵਤ ਹ:
The saints eternally dwell in the company of the devout, absorbed in celestial love, singing praises of the Divine. This describes a state of being where constant remembrance of naam transforms the mind, creating an unbroken connection with the Divine through the sangat. The image of being "dyed in beautiful color" represents this complete absorption, where worldly attachment maya no longer holds sway.

Themes: devotion, divine love, remembrance, spiritual community, absorption, praise, transformation, liberation
ਕਾਢਿ ਲੀਏ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਆਨ ਬਿਖੈ ਤੇ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਮਨੁ ਲਾਵ:
This is a plea for divine intervention to rescue the mind from worldly corruption and attach it to the sangat (the company of the devout). The speaker acknowledges God's role in transforming human consciousness, pulling individuals from various vices and establishing them in the company of the holy. This line functions as both a supplication and a declaration of spiritual dependence, seeking refuge in the Divine to overcome maya (worldly attachment).

Themes: divine rescue, attachment to the sangat, overcoming vice, transformation of consciousness, supplication, refuge in God, maya, spiritual dependence
ਮਹਿਮਾ ਸਾਧੂ ਸੰਗ ਕੀ ਸੁਨਹੁ ਮੇਰੇ ਮੀਤਾ ॥:
The line declares the supreme glory of sangat (the company of the devout) as the highest attainment, instructing the listener to pay close attention to this truth. It positions sangat as the essential means to connect with the Divine, emphasizing its transformative power and the spiritual elevation it brings. The term "mitra" (friends) creates an intimate tone, making this a direct, urgent instruction about the path to liberation.

Themes: sangat, divine glory, spiritual community, remembrance, devotion, instruction, friendship, elevation
ਮੇਰਾ ਗੁਰੁ ਪਰਮੇਸਰੁ ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ॥:
This declaration establishes the Guru as the embodiment of the Divine, who is the ultimate source of all comfort and well-being. It positions the Guru not merely as a teacher but as the very presence of the Transcendent Lord, whose nature is to bestow peace and remove suffering. This identification of the Guru with the Giver of peace is a foundational assertion of refuge and surrender.

Themes: Divine presence, Guru as embodiment, source of peace, ultimate comfort, refuge, surrender, Transcendent Lord, well-being.
ਤੁਮ ਦਾਤੇ ਤੁਮ ਪੁਰਖ ਬਿਧਾਤੇ ॥:
This line declares the Divine as both the Creator and the Sustainer, establishing God's dual role as the origin of all life and the source of all provision. It affirms that existence itself is a gift from the Divine, who both brings beings into being and cares for them. The Creator is also the Provider, making divine grace the foundation of all life.

Themes: Creator, Provider, Divine Grace, Sustainer, Origin of Life, Giver of Gifts
ਕਰੁਣਾ ਮੈ ਕਿਰਪਾਲ ਕ੍ਰਿਪਾ ਨਿਧਿ ਜੀਵਨ ਪਦ ਨਾਨਕ: This line declares the Divine as the source of all mercy and compassion, the ultimate refuge for the suffering. It states that through experiencing the Divine vision, one attains the highest spiritual life, a state of liberation and fulfillment. The teeka emphasizes this vision as granting an elevated status to the soul, a redemption achieved in this lifetime. Themes: Divine mercy, spiritual liberation, blessed vision, refuge, compassion, elevated existence, life's purpose.
ਤੂੰ ਭਾਰੋ ਠਾਕੁਰੁ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੇਰਾ ॥੨॥:
The Divine is the foundation of all existence, the profound repository of all virtues and qualities. This line establishes the Divine as the ultimate source of excellence and the essential support for all creation, emphasizing boundless depth and perfection. It declares the Divine as the treasure of all virtues and the Great Lord who upholds everything.

Themes: Divine perfection, foundation of existence, repository of virtues, ultimate support, boundless depth, treasure of excellence, Great Lord, source of all qualities.
ਦੇਵਣਹਾਰੁ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ ਕਿਤੁ ਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਲਾਹੀਐ ॥:
The line expresses the inadequacy of human language to praise the Divine, who is the ultimate giver and sustainer of all life. It establishes a relationship of profound humility, acknowledging that the Creator's generosity is so vast that no tongue can adequately express gratitude or offer sufficient worship. This is not a question seeking an answer but a rhetorical statement about the infinite nature of the Divine and the limitations of mortal expression.

Themes: divine generosity, human limitation, inadequacy of praise, humility before the Creator, infinite nature of God, gratitude, worship, speechlessness before the divine
ਤੇਰੇ ਕਵਨ ਕਵਨ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਗਾਵਾ ਤੂ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਗ:
The devotee questions which of the Divine's innumerable virtues to praise, acknowledging the Divine as the ultimate Lord and the inexhaustible source of all qualities. This is an expression of awe before the infinite majesty of the Divine, recognizing human language as inadequate to capture the totality of divine perfection. The devotee positions themselves as a humble singer before the treasure of excellence.

Themes: divine attributes, inadequacy of language, humility before the infinite, worship through praise, Lord and master, treasure of qualities
ਰੇ ਬਉਰੇ ਤੁਹਿ ਘਰੀ ਨ ਰਾਖੈ ਕੋਈ ॥: This is a stark warning to the deluded mind that worldly attachments offer no true refuge; no one will protect you from the consequences of your own ignorance, not even for a moment. The divine presence is the only shelter, and abandoning it is to abandon safety itself. Themes: delusion, refuge, divine protection, worldly attachment, consequences of ignorance, true shelter.
ਕਾਹੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਡੋਲਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਮਨਸਾ ਪੂਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥:
The mind questions its own instability when the Divine is the complete fulfiller of all wishes and intentions. This line admonishes the mind for doubt, asserting that surrender to the Divine Name (naam) resolves uncertainty. The Lord is the one who actualizes all heartfelt aspirations, making wavering illogical. The mind finds stability only in this recognition.

Themes: mind's wavering, divine fulfiller, surrender to naam, overcoming doubt, stability in devotion, heart's fulfillment
ਰੇ ਮਨ ਤੂ ਭੀ ਭਜੁ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ॥੨॥:
The mind is commanded to engage in simran, vibrating upon the Divine as an act of surrender and devotion. This is an instruction to redirect the mind's focus from worldly distractions to naam, establishing a relationship with the Creator through loving remembrance. The mind's purpose is to find its home in the Divine presence.

Themes: mind's redirection, simran practice, surrender to the Divine, naam meditation, escaping worldly attachment, finding refuge in the Creator, spiritual discipline, inner focus.
ਮਨ ਮੇਰਿਆ ਅੰਤਰਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਨਿਧਾਨੁ ਹੈ ਬਾਹਰਿ ਵਸਤੁ:
This line instructs the mind to recognize the divine treasure within itself rather than seeking fulfillment in external objects. It admonishes against worldly attachment (maya) by declaring that true abundance resides internally. The mind is directed inward to discover the divine presence, shifting focus from external searching to internal realization. The treasure represents both the divine Name (naam) and the state of union with the Divine.

Themes: inner treasure, mind's focus, divine presence within, rejection of external search, maya, naam, self-discovery
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਤੂ ਕਾਏ ਦੇਖਿ ਭੁਲਾਨਾ ॥:
This is a direct address to the deluded mind, questioning its attachment to the world. The speaker calls the listener a "madman" for being captivated by maya (worldly attachment), which causes one to forget life's true purpose. The line functions as a sharp rebuke, awakening the mind to its own folly in pursuing transient things over the eternal divine. It describes a state of spiritual blindness where the divine is ignored for the ephemeral.

Themes: delusion, worldly attachment, spiritual awakening, divine remembrance, human folly, maya, distraction from truth
ਸੁਣਿ ਬਾਵਰੇ ਥੀਉ ਰੇਣੁ ਜਿਨੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥:
This is an urgent command to abandon ego and embrace humility as the path to union with the Divine. The "madman" is anyone who seeks God without first becoming the dust at the feet of those who practice naam simran. True realization comes not from pride but from complete surrender to the devoted. The image of dust signifies both ultimate humility and the merging of the self with the Divine.

Themes: humility, surrender, devotion, naam simran, ego dissolution, spiritual path, dust metaphor, Divine union
ਲਖ ਖੁਸੀਆ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀਆ ਜੇ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇਇ:
This line describes the incomprehensible bliss that arises from the Guru's grace, framing it as a royal pleasure surpassing all worldly delights. It declares that divine favor is the sole source of true contentment, transforming the seeker's experience from lack to abundance. The Guru's glance is both a concrete image of divine attention and the mechanism of spiritual liberation.

Themes: divine grace, spiritual bliss, Guru's favor, contentment, liberation from desire, royal metaphor, divine attention
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥:
The True Guru's mercy eliminates suffering by reframing all experiences as divine will. This state is achieved through naam and simran, where the devotee's perception transforms, recognizing maya as the Guru's play. The Guru's compassion is not emotional but a power that dissolves the disciple's identification with pain.

Themes: Guru's mercy, elimination of suffering, transformation of perception, divine will, naam, simran, maya
ਹਰਿ ਚਉਥੜੀ ਲਾਵ ਮਨਿ ਸਹਜੁ ਭਇਆ ਹਰਿ ਪਾਇਆ ਬਲਿ:
The mind achieves profound stillness through the divine union, finding complete refuge in the Lord. This state of spiritual absorption is the result of divine grace, a surrender that brings inner peace and liberation from worldly attachment. The marriage ceremony symbolizes this sacred union with the Divine.

Themes: divine union, spiritual stillness, surrender to the Divine, liberation from maya, grace of the Lord, inner peace, absorption in naam, refuge in the Divine.
ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਨਾਇ ॥:
The mind finds peace by internalizing the Guru's wisdom, which grants all desired fruits. This is not external appeasement but an internal state of surrender where the Guru's presence becomes the source of contentment, transforming the seeker's consciousness and fulfilling all spiritual and worldly needs through this divine connection.

Themes: Guru's presence, internal peace, divine wisdom, surrender, fulfillment of desires, transformation of consciousness
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਮੇਰਾ ਸਦਾ ਸਹਾਈ ਜਿਨਿ ਦੁਖ ਕਾ ਕਾਟਿਆ:
This line declares the Guru as the eternal destroyer of suffering, cutting at its root rather than merely alleviating symptoms. It establishes the Guru as the constant support for those who seek refuge, framing the relationship as one where the Guru actively eliminates pain's source. The Guru's help is not temporary relief but permanent destruction of suffering's foundation.

Themes: Guru as destroyer of suffering, eternal refuge, root cause elimination, divine support, liberation from pain, Guru's protective grace.
ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਮਿਲਣ ਕੀ ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰੀਆ ॥:
This is the human purpose: a singular opportunity for union with the Divine. The line declares this encounter as the ultimate purpose of life, framing existence as a chance for spiritual realization. It instructs the seeker to recognize this moment as the sole reason for being, urging immediate action toward this goal before the opportunity passes. This is the core of the path: naam (the divine Name) is the means, and this union is the destination.

Themes: divine purpose, human opportunity, spiritual union, singular chance, divine encounter, life's meaning, seeking the Lord, now or never
ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ ਤੂੰ ਆਇਆ ਲਾਹਾ ਲੈਣਿ ॥:
This line addresses the human condition as a purposeful journey to attain naam (the divine Name) as the ultimate profit. It frames mortal existence not as random chance but as a deliberate quest for spiritual gain, distinguishing this profit from worldly pursuits. The instruction is clear: recognize the true purpose of life and direct all efforts toward this divine acquisition.

Themes: human purpose, spiritual profit, divine seeking, mortal existence, naam as wealth, intentional life journey
ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤਿ ਦ੍ਰਿੜੁ ਮਿਲੁ ਸਾਧ ਨਾਨਕ ਤੇਰੈ ਕਾਮਿ:
This line declares that encountering the Divine and establishing firm devotional worship within the heart is the sole purpose and effective action for human life. It instructs the seeker to make this devotion unwavering, as this connection with the Divine is the only work that truly matters and will bear fruit. The line emphasizes that this devotional focus is the essential task for spiritual fulfillment.

Themes: divine encounter, unwavering devotion, heart-centered worship, sole purpose, effective action, spiritual fulfillment, naam, simran
ਜੀਵਨਾ ਸਫਲ ਜੀਵਨ ਸੁਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ ਸਦ ਜੀਵਨਾ:
This line defines successful life as continuous engagement with the Divine through hearing and chanting naam, resulting in eternal existence. It instructs that true life is found in simran, the loving remembrance of the Divine Name, which transcends mortal limitations and grants spiritual permanence. The line establishes a clear criterion for a life well-lived: constant absorption in naam.

Themes: eternal life, divine remembrance, successful existence, spiritual permanence, naam meditation, hearing the Divine, transcending mortality, continuous devotion
